references.text: The Lord looked with favor on Abel's offering, which recalls God's acceptance of the sacrifice when the flame rose from the altar.
Fire went out from the Lord and consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and the people fell on their faces, just as Manoah and his wife did.
Elijah was taken up to heaven, which recalls the angel's ascent in the flame from the altar.
The Lord's angel touched the offering with the staff, fire broke out from the rock, and the angel vanished from Gideon's sight, which is a clear parallel to the event with Manoah.
Isaiah fell down in awe when he saw the Lord's glory, just as Manoah and his wife fell on their faces.
Isaiah's vision of the Lord in the temple shows a similar awe and worship that Manoah and his wife experienced.
John fell down as dead when he saw the glorified Christ, a reaction that reflects Manoah and his wife's awe.
